title: First-mile surge simulation and KPI sensitivity report
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Quick working brief for ’first mile’ (first 72 hours) of a staged public rollout.
- Focus: surge capacity simulations, KPI sensitivity sweeps, staffing rotas for triage, and immediate launch readiness checklist.
- Audience: product-ops, release-eng, SRE, oncall leads, customer-success triage.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline traffic projection (week 0 ramp): 120k requests/day, mean tokens per request 140.
- Run three surge scenarios: conservative (+2x baseline), probable (+5x), worst (+12x peak bursts).
- Key KPIs to watch: error-rate (5xx) >0.5%, p95 latency >750ms, token cost burn rate >1.8x forecast.
- Staffing: prepare 48h surge pool (14 people across eng/ops/CS), escalate to 72h surge (36 people) if sustained >5x for >6 hours.

Simulation summary (numbers are approximate — see attached sheet draft):
- Inputs:
  - Baseline RPS: 1.4 (120k/day)
  - Mean tokens/request: 140
  - Model mix: 60% base Llama-variant q4_0, 30% redwood-verified-medium, 10% fallback small-quantized
  - Typical seq lengths: mean 180, 95th 420
  - Batching efficiency: default 1.2x token throughput under steady-state, drops to 1.05x under bursty traffic

- Scenarios:
  1) Conservative (2x): sustained 240k/day for 72h, peak hourly 25% above sustained. Expected p95 latency bump to ~420ms, cost burn ~1.9x baseline. No data loss expected if autoscale policy + burst nodes enabled.
  2) Probable (5x): sustained 600k/day for 48h with short spikes. p95 latency climbs to ~900ms without emergency batching tweaks; potential token-cost burn 3.5x. Risk: KV cache warm-up causes early request drop rate ~0.2% during first 6h.
  3) Worst (12x burst): multi-hour 12x spikes (1–3h) + baseline returns. If fallback routing not enabled, expect cascading queueing and model rejections; immediate mitigation requires canary-fallthrough to smaller model (cost up, latency down) and traffic shaping.

KPI sensitivity matrix (how small changes move key signals):
- Error rate sensitivity:
  - +10% average seq length -> +0.15% 5xx chance (tokens/timeouts)
  - +20% RPS -> +0.45% 5xx unless batch reconfiguration enabled
- Latency sensitivity:
  - p95 latency is most sensitive to # of concurrent requests per GPU and batch effectiveness. Reducing batch window from 40ms -> 15ms increases p95 by ~220ms in simulation.
- Cost sensitivity:
  - Model mix shift 10% from medium to small -> ~12% reduction in token cost but quality risk for generated outputs.

Operational guardrails and thresholds (for automated alerts / runbook steps):
- Green -> Amber -> Red thresholds (first 72h):
  - 5xx rate: green <0.2%, amber 0.2%–0.5% (investigate), red >0.5% -> open incident channel
  - p95 latency (user-facing): green <350ms, amber 350–700ms, red >700ms -> consider model fallback routing
  - Token burn vs forecast: green <1.2x forecast, amber 1.2–1.8x, red >1.8x -> throttle non-critical routes, enable cheaper quantized models
  - Cache warm-up errors: >0.1% new-user traffic for >4h -> add pre-warm policy for KV prefixes

Staffing playbook (first 0–72h):
- Roles and responsibilities:
  - Launch commander (product-ops): Priya Menon (primary), Ethan Cole (backup)
  - SRE lead: Xiao Chen -> hardware scaling, autoscaler oversight
  - Serving runtime lead: Rafael Ortiz -> model routing, batching knobs
  - CS strike team: Marisol Diaz -> customer triage and top-customer comms

- Rota plan (sketch):
  - Phase A (hours 0–12): core oncall + launch commander + CS onsite (total ~10 people)
  - Phase B (12–36h): expand to 24 people rotating 4h shifts (eng + sres + ops)
  - Phase C (36–72h): maintain surge pool (14–18) for monitoring and bugfixing, scale down if amber signals resolved for 12h

Immediate runbook actions (quick checklist):
- Pre-roll (before traffic ramp):
  - Verify autoscale policies include burst_nodes and gpu_autoprobe (OWNER: Xiao)
  - Smoke test canary route to fallback_small_model (OWNER: Rafael)
  - Confirm marketplace quotas and Dedicated reserve pool unlocked (OWNER: Priya)
  - Upload final traffic plan to #launch-ops Slack and set pinned message (OWNER: Marisol)

- On amber alert:
  - Triage with SRE -> identify whether queuing or model error (OWNER: Xiao)
  - Flip traffic -> 70% to medium, 30% to small for 15 minutes to test capacity (OWNER: Rafael)
  - Inform CS for any impacted enterprise customers (OWNER: Marisol)

- On red alert:
  - Open incident, call in full surge pool, enable emergency fallbacks, throttle background routes, and prioritize sessions for enterprise (OWNERS: Priya / Xiao)
  - If token burn >2.2x forecast, engage finance (billing guard) to start charge checkpointing and customer notifications

Open questions / TODOs (items we need to finalize before signoff):
- Finalize per-route priority list (which routes are non-critical and can be throttled). Current draft: embeddings low-priority, large-batch-rerank mid, chat core high. Need product signoff. (JIRA:POPS-4823)
- Confirm Dedicated reserve pool growth plan and activation time (expected 18–22 min to provision additional nodes). Can we reduce to <10m? (ACTION: infra + release-eng)
- Validate telemetry retention window for first-mile analytics. 90d is expensive; propose 30d for high-res metrics and 14d for raw traces. (ACTION: observability)
- Create a short canned customer message templates for CS for amber and red signals (ACTION: Marisol).

Appendix A — snapshot of spreadsheet (plain text view)
- columns: scenario | peak_mult | sustained_day | est_p95_ms | est_5xx_pct | est_cost_mult | staffing_needed_48h
- row1: baseline | 1x | 120k | 300 | 0.05% | 1.0x | 10
- row2: conservative | 2x | 240k | 420 | 0.12% | 1.9x | 14
- row3: probable | 5x | 600k | 900 | 0.45% | 3.5x | 36
- row4: worst | 12x | burst | 1600+ | 1.8% | 6.8x | 72+

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is a working simulation: numbers tuned from last-year telemetry and serve-runtime bench runs. Treat as conservative on latency and optimistic on scaling speed.
- Please comment inline on route-priority and critical-customer lists.
- If you have suggestions for automated mitigation strategies (e.g., token-budget based soft-throttles per API key), flag them — we should capture as potential Optimize feature workstream.

Change log:
